selection_reasoning: These two tasks form a natural multi-hop dependency chain in Minecraft. To craft a wooden sword, the player needs wooden planks, which come from logs obtained by chopping trees. The sequence is: chop trees → obtain logs → convert logs to planks → craft planks into sticks and combine with planks to craft a wooden sword. This is a coherent, observable, and verifiable chain that doesn't require deep Minecraft domain knowledge beyond basic crafting. The dependency is genuine — without chopping trees first, the player has no materials to craft the sword.

edges.reason: Crafting a wooden sword requires planks and sticks, both derived from logs obtained by chopping trees

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because chopping an oak tree causes oak_log items to drop into the player's inventory. The player starts with an empty inventory, so any oak_log present confirms tree chopping occurred. Note: if the player converts all logs to planks, this check would fail on current inventory — but milestones are latched once achieved, so this is acceptable.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a wooden sword places it directly into the player's inventory. The player starts with no wooden_sword, so its presence confirms the full crafting chain was completed (logs → planks → sticks → wooden sword via crafting table). This is the most direct and reliable check for a crafting task.

scene_description: A cleared grass area with two oak trees (4 logs each) for chopping and a crafting table for crafting a wooden sword. The area is cleared of obstructions above to ensure the player can easily navigate between trees and crafting table. The scene supports the full crafting chain: chop oak logs → convert to planks (inventory 2x2) → craft sticks (inventory 2x2) → craft wooden sword (crafting table 3x3).
task_text: Chop one of the oak trees to collect logs, then use the crafting table to craft a wooden sword.

design_notes.scene_layout: Two oak trees with 4 logs each (8 total logs = 32 planks; only 3 planks needed for a wooden sword). Tree 1 at ~4,1-4,0 (east of spawn). Tree 2 at ~-3,1-4,4 (northwest of spawn). Crafting table at ~5,1,5 (southeast corner). First command clears a 17x10x17 air volume above the platform to remove natural trees from the biome. Grass platform (11x11) provides a flat walking surface.
design_notes.player_start_state: Empty inventory, standing on grass platform at center. Must punch logs by hand (~4 seconds per log).
design_notes.crafting_chain: Oak log → 4 oak planks (2x2 inventory grid) → 2 planks + 2 planks = 4 sticks (2x2 inventory grid) → 2 planks + 1 stick = wooden sword (3x3 crafting table required for 1x3 vertical recipe).
design_notes.material_budget: 1 tree (4 logs) yields 16 planks. Wooden sword needs 2 planks + 1 stick (from 2 planks) = 3 planks total. Massive surplus ensures task is completable even with mistakes.
known_considerations: Milestone 1 (chop_trees) checks inventory for oak_log — if player converts all logs to planks before evaluation, milestone may not be currently satisfied. Assumes latched milestone evaluation.
Natural biome trees may be visible beyond the 8-block clearing radius but placed trees are closest and most obvious targets.
No tools given — hand-punching logs is standard early-game Minecraft and takes ~4 seconds per block.
